title: Production Tool: shared definitions
description: Types every other contract uses. Contract version 3 (2026-10-13, features/contract-v3.clan): id-keyed maps, ranks, camera fields, beats, links with one rule table, asks, the crew, tenants and people, formats, and the decision-tree addresses.

sha256.description: Content address of an artifact: the SHA-256 of its bytes. Authoritative; every URL is only a hint.

id.description: Prefixed ULID made by the client (or, for a job's question, the relay): job_, ref_, key_, shot_, beat_, scene_, script_, storyboard_, video_, frame_, take_, render_, rev_, link_, board_, sketch_, doc_, fset_, size_, check_, q_, sug_, spin_, stale_, exp_, edl_, node_, proj_ …. Never holds '.', '[', ']' or '#', so it is always a safe map key and address segment.

sceneId.description: An Excalidraw element id on the canvas (a group, a note or an ink group): owned by the canvas, never by the document. Never holds '.', '[', ']' or '#'.

tag.description: A ref's wire name inside one provider job, in the strictest form any provider accepts (Runway: 3-16 chars). The relay derives it from the ref's name (relay/names.py).

key.description: A solid reference key: one character, place or object (maya, lamp, loc). Lowercase letters and digits only: the underscore separates key from variant.

variant.description: Free text after the key: front, side, laughing, red-coat. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

refName.description: key_variant, as a person writes it after @ (maya_laughing). Unique in a document.

subject.description: A name after @ in words sent to the relay: a bare key is the whole character (its front plus up to 3 other variants), key_variant one look.

ratio.description: The ratios a person picks for a storyboard, a video or a sketch area. A format's exact shape is an aspect, never a new ratio.

clipQuality.description: A clip's quality (features/clip-quality.clan): draft is the cheapest size the model makes, standard 720p (the size before quality existed), final the best it makes up to 1080p. The size each means per model is the capability sheet's ops[op].quality.

aspect.description: An exact shape in whole units (1080 x 1920, 1.91:1 as 191 x 100). Used where a format's shape is not one of the four ratios.

rank.description: A fractional order key (rocicorp/fractional-indexing, base 62). The only order of scenes, shots, beats, boards, sizes and cut items: a move is one write to one rank. clan-store/src/rank.ts and relay/rank.py make the same keys (examples/ranks.json).

cameraSize.description: graphic: a shot with no camera, such as the end card ('Graphic · Static').

camera.description: A shot's camera, every part its own single-value field (a patch per leaf).

cameraPatch.description: A change to a shot's camera (frame_edit's frameEdit.camera): the leaves of camera, none required, each the new value. size never becomes graphic (a graphic card has no camera to change).

cameraWords.description: How each camera value is said (features/frame-change-edit.clan): label is the word the camera chips and the diff show ('angle: eye level -> overhead'); words are the phrases that mean it (the longest match wins). One table for the web's labels, director.v7's camera lines (the <!-- camera-words --> marker), the passthrough's lexicon and the eval, so they never differ. Every value of cameraSize, cameraAngle, cameraMovement and movementSpeed has a row (a contract test holds it).

beatKind.description: moment: something that happens at a time in the shot. line: spoken on screen (speaker, parenthetical, tied to a moment or not). vo, music, sound: the audio rows. camera: a change of camera inside the shot.

crewId.description: The crew (ui-behaviour 5.1): Dex directs, Skye scripts, Fin films, Rhea retouches, Edie edits; Nell notes and Jude judges are the house agents. Stable ids: the names on screen may change, these do not (wren is Fin, ellis is Nell).

tenantId.description: The agency: napkin-web's TenantId (UUIDv5 of 'napkin:agency:<agency>'). Opaque here.

personRef.description: A person, as the decision chain names them: human:<personId> (the participantId from GET /me). Opaque here.

actorRef.description: Who wrote something: a person (human:<id>) or a crew member (dex, skye, …).

address.description: <doc-id>#<entity-keyed path> (docs/contracts/os-layer.md §3): shots[shot_X].camera.size, frames[frame_Y]. What a decision targets or cites.

decisionId.description: A decision in the chain (clan-sdk DECISION_ID_PREFIX).

formatId.description: A format in format-packs.json: lowercase, digits, dots and hyphens (linkedin-image-1.91x1). Never contains '/'. Never a map key or a path segment (it may hold a dot): sizes are their own entities and carry it as a value.

formatRef.description: Which format a size or a sketch area was made for, and from which version of its pack. A copy: the values that matter (aspect, delivery, bleed, safe area) are copied beside it at creation.

client_id.description: Set when the pack is a client's own (their library shelf).

safeArea.description: format-packs.json safe_area: insets from each edge, or a centred live box.

refRole.description: What a reference is for (ui-behaviour 3.6). An open set in meaning: a ref may add its own label. What Dex takes from each role is refRoleTable.

refRoleTable.description: One line per role, shown in the role picker (ui_line) and written into the director's prompt (prompt_line) verbatim, so the UI and the prompt never differ. views: whether the role gets a front and turnaround views. payload: what a ref of this role holds (image: an asset; swatches; font; rule; document). picker: main (one of the ten pills) or more.

character.ui_line: Dex keeps who they are: face, build and look
character.prompt_line: character reference: keep this person's identity, face, build and look

location.prompt_line: location reference: set the scene in this place

lighting.prompt_line: lighting reference: match its light only

composition.prompt_line: composition reference: follow its framing and camera position only

product.prompt_line: product reference: show this exact product; keep its shape, label and colours

style.ui_line: Dex matches its look and finish
style.prompt_line: style reference: match its look, palette and finish, not its content

wardrobe.prompt_line: wardrobe reference: match the clothes only

pose.prompt_line: pose reference: copy the body pose only

prop.prompt_line: prop reference: include this object as it looks

texture.prompt_line: texture reference: match the surface and material only

colour.prompt_line: colour reference: take its colours only

layout.ui_line: Dex follows where things sit, not how they look
layout.prompt_line: layout reference: follow where things sit, not how they look

logo.ui_line: Dex places the logo as drawn, never redrawn
logo.prompt_line: logo reference: reproduce this logo exactly; never redraw or restyle it

palette.prompt_line: brand palette: keep to these colours

typography.ui_line: Dex sets type in this font
typography.prompt_line: typography: set any type in this font and weight

brand_rule.ui_line: Dex follows the rule; Jude checks it

document.ui_line: Dex reads it as background only
document.prompt_line: background document: use it as context only, never as text on screen

other.ui_line: Dex uses it as you describe in the label
other.prompt_line: reference: use as the label says

view.description: op view: the turnaround view to make from the source image, and the variant the result is named by.

region.description: A box in 0-1 coordinates of the image it sits on, origin top-left.

linkEndpointKind.description: What a link joins. group, note and ink are canvas things: their id is a sceneId. Every other kind is a document entity: its id is the entity's id. key (2026-10-15, owner): a solid key (keys[id]), the whole character or thing; every named ref with that key, each of its views, is in a node's scope through the one link. text (2026-10-16, owner): a text written on the canvas (texts[id], which holds its words and its canvas element); linked into a node, its words are that node's input words.

linkRole.description: A link's label (ui-behaviour 3.4). A reference's link carries its role (character, lighting, …); 'layout' is both a ref role and a shot's layout guide.

linkRule.description: Every link that may exist (ui-behaviour 3.4), the one table the canvas's canLink(), clan-store's integrity check and check.py read. A link is allowed when a rule has its from kind, its to kind and its role; the first such rule decides its limits. per_target one: at most one link of that role into one target. per_source one: at most one link from one source into one target. system: made only by the tool. generating: the nodes that send work to an agent. Refused besides: a link into a ref, a document or a brand board; a link out of a video except as a format set's master; a link that makes a loop.

questionOption.description: One button under a question (the Research tool's question_option, app/templates/campaign-research/schema.json). With a value it proceeds with that value; without one it is the escape that opens the text box, and the answer is sent as text. detail and cost are said under the label ('6 shots · about $1.20 for frames').

routeValue.description: An option that sends the work somewhere: plan the storyboard first, link a script. node is the node it goes to, when there is one.

question.description: What an agent asks instead of guessing (ui-behaviour 3.17), the Research tool's question with three additions: kind, recommended_option_id and per-option detail and cost. block: no option proceeds until one is done. nudge: at least one proceeds; one may be recommended. ambiguity: the words could mean two things; nothing is recommended. A job's question id is minted by the relay.

address.description: The field the answer settles, when it settles one.

answer.description: A person's answer: an option id or text, never both.

provider.description: A provider the relay can route to.

madeBy.description: The provider that made an output, as recorded at the time. Free, not the routing enum.

op.description: generate: a new image from 1-14 inputs. view: a turnaround view. shot_list: Dex plans shots from a script (no provider). frame: a storyboard frame. region_edit: edit inside a region of a still. clip: frame to video. clip_edit: change a clip. stitch: render the ad. frame_edit: change this frame. clip_patch: fix a moment's window and splice it. bridge: a clip between two shots. cutout: Rhea's cut-out. transcribe: Nell reads ink. write: Skye drafts or rewrites. read: Nell reads a document. check: Jude judges a result. resize: Make all sizes on a still. cutdown: a video cut-down. upscale: Rhea upscales. Ops with no builder yet answer 422 capability_missing.

quotaClass.description: Which daily quota an op draws on: opQuotaClass.

opQuotaClass.description: The quota class of every op.

jobState.description: needs_input: an agent asked (Job.question) and the job waits, uncharged and never timing out into a guess, until someone answers or stops it. uncertain: the provider may have accepted the job with no id recorded; reconciled by querying, never by paying again.

cost.description: Three separate numbers, never inferred from each other. confirmed stays absent and unknown true until the provider reports it.

mime.description: The kinds of file the tool keeps: pictures (SVG for logos), clips, audio, brand books (PDF), documents (DOCX), fonts, Fountain or plain text, and zips.

assetRef.description: An artifact passed between browser, relay and provider. url is our CloudFront input path from POST /uploads.

output.description: One result of a job, already copied into our S3 (the provider URL is never handed out). An image output always carries its measured w and h; one centre-cropped to the job's shape (input.aspect, else input.ratio) also carries croppedFrom.

croppedFrom.description: The model's size before the relay centre-cropped the picture to the job's shape (1344 x 768 for a 16:9 job that came back 1344 x 756). The uncropped original is kept.

message.description: One line a person can read in the node.

providerCode.description: The provider's own code, for logs.
